newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker with U.S. but outperform.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker with U.S. but outperform.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed softer on Thursday, pulled lower by weakness in U.S. treasuries, even as the recent rally in the Canadian dollar helped Canadian bonds to outperform, analysts said.

"In Canada we're just following the U.S. It wasn't particularly active today," said David Yu, fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "In light of what happened to the U.S., our market just came off with it."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.35 to C$108.05 to yield 7.306 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 15/32 to yield 6.83 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 48 basis points from 49 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

While Canada's dollar closed almost flat at C$1.3411 (US$0.7457) from Wednesday's close, the currency rose by more than a full Canadian cent on Wednesday. Most of Wednesday's buying interest came from Europe after a bullish story on Canada in Britain's Financial Times newspaper.
Yu said Canada's outperformance was likely linked to the recent strength in the dollar and the foreign buying of Canadian bonds it sparked.

Among new issues, the Bank of Montreal said on Thursday that it planned to issue C$250 million in series 24 debentures due in April, 2007. The interest on the issue is payable semi-annually at a fixed rate of 6.05 percent until April, 2002, the bank said.

Hydro-Quebec set a C$400 million 5.75 percent bond due February 15, 2002 in financial markets. The bond was priced at C$99.22 with a yield of 5.93 percent, 9.3 basis points over the benchmark government bond. The new issue also contains a feature which allows the holder to exchange it at maturity for a 10-year Hydro-Quebec bond.
